key_insight: Retired DDR4 is a real near-term supply buffer: zero wafer starts, ~10-20% of new-bit cost, and shipping CXL controllers already accept DDR4.
killer_doubt: Already deployed at hyperscale. As a capacity tier it adds ~70-100 ns over local DRAM, and 5-7-year-old DDR4 (HCfirst ~10k, VRT drift) needs controller-side mitigation.
decisive_experiment: Nothing is needed to prove the concept. For the supply model, burn-in 1,000 retired RDIMMs (~$50k): failure, retention-bin and HCfirst rates, plus a census of decommissioned DDR4 GB/yr.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024) reuses DDR4 behind CXL. Marvell Structera and Astera Leo support DDR4 reuse (prior knowledge).

key_insight: Draw-stack-redraw-slice makes ~1e7 vias/cm2 in one thermal process. A fine-pitch, alignment-free z-axis wire slab could forgive registration errors in die-block bonding (I-02164).
killer_doubt: Molten ~1 um Cu cores Rayleigh-break in ~0.1-1 s in the draw neck. Cu/borosilicate CTE (17 vs 3.3 ppm/K) gives ~0.7% cool-down strain. Bundle jitter >0.5 um/cm.
decisive_experiment: At a university fiber tower (~$150k), draw a 3-stage Cu-in-borosilicate preform and a hollow MCP-glass preform to be Cu-plated later. Slice to 100 um. Measure via continuity on 1e5 vias by X-ray CT, plus resistance and positional jitter.
prior_art: Taylor-Ulitovsky glass-coated microwire. Microchannel-plate draw-stack-slice (Photonis, Incom). Iterative-draw nanowire arrays (Bayindir group, 2011). LPKF LIDE laser TGVs. Applied to interposers: none found.

key_insight: A polished laminated-die-block edge gives TSV-free, interposer-free memory-on-logic: ~5k pads per die ≈ 2.5 TB/s. The gaps form a microchannel heat sink (~5 K at 1 W/mm2).
killer_doubt: Pads exist only in the ~3-5 um DRAM BEOL strip (~5-10k per 10 mm edge, not 250k). Thickness variation over 100 dies accumulates ~±10 um, against ~0.5 um bond overlay.
decisive_experiment: Laminate 16-32 plasma-diced daisy-chain dies and CMP the block edge. Add an adaptive RDL (or the I-10449 slab). Bond to a logic test die at 10, then 3 um pitch. Measure yield and ΔT at 1 W/mm2 (~$600k).
prior_art: Irvine Sensors / 3D-Plus edge-metallized die cubes (prior knowledge). Die-edge interconnect patents (US 12211799 family, via search snippet). Standing memory dies on logic: none found.

key_insight: Rotation turns rare catastrophic flips into dense small noise. That helps outlier-sensitive nonlinear steps (softmax, top-k, max-inner-product) and could let ECC-paid arrays (N-62) relax margin for AI tensors.
killer_doubt: Rotation conserves error energy. At 1% BER on int8, spread noise σ≈15 LSB vs ~30 LSB signal (SNR ≈6 dB). Only ~1e-3 works, and no high-BER DRAM SKU exists.
decisive_experiment: Software only (<$20k GPU): inject 1e-4 to 1e-2 BER into int8 KV caches, embedding tables and ANN indexes. Compare plain, Hadamard-spread and MSB-only-ECC. Report the accuracy-vs-BER knee and the refresh or capacitor relaxation each knee allows.
prior_art: EDEN approximate DRAM for DNNs (MICRO 2019). Flikker (ASPLOS 2011). QuaRot/SpinQuant Hadamard rotations (2024). Bit-error spreading for stored embeddings: none found.

key_insight: With independent tier failures, ~87% of failed 12-high stacks (75% yield) have one bad die. Sold at 11/12 capacity (like H200's 141/144 GB), that recovers ~+18% bits.
killer_doubt: Many stack rejects are TSV power shorts, base-die faults, warpage or underfill voids that cannot be fused out. If >50% are, the gain falls below ~+7% HBM supply.
decisive_experiment: Through a vendor partnership (~$300k), run failure analysis on ~500 rejected HBM stacks and classify each as tier-fusable or stack-level. Prototype base-die remap firmware and qualify one 11/12-capacity SKU.
prior_art: JEDEC HBM lane repair and spare TSVs. GPU-level harvesting (H100 enables 5 of 6 stacks). Vendor lower bins (prior knowledge). Public tier-fuse re-binning: none found.

key_insight: Summary keys in HBM with full KV in a capacity tier has the right shape: it moves KV out of HBM, which uses ~3x the wafer per bit.
killer_doubt: Already published and open-sourced. The tier link is a bound: fetching 2k tokens x ~327 KB over a 64 GB/s CXL x16 link takes ~10 ms per decode step.
decisive_experiment: Nothing is needed. Reproduce Quest or ShadowKV with a CXL-tier offload on LongBench/RULER and measure the HBM footprint against tokens/s (<$20k).

key_insight: Bank-parallel row buffers give ~8x the external bandwidth (~17 TB/s per stack). Scoring INT4 keys there and returning only indices lets KV live in a DDR/LPDDR tier, not HBM.
killer_doubt: Software top-k (Quest/ShadowKV) already cuts KV traffic ~8-16x. In-memory filtering only removes the low-bit key scan (~1/8 of KV). Bank-PIM cost Samsung ~50% of PIM-die capacity.
decisive_experiment: Trace-driven study (<$150k): Llama-70B-class model on LongBench/RULER, comparing software Quest with in-bank INT4 top-k on a DDR5/LPDDR-PIM tier (Ramulator plus DRAMPower). Add area of the INT4 MAC and top-k in a 3-metal DRAM-like PDK.
prior_art: SK hynix AiM, Samsung HBM-PIM, AttAcc (ASPLOS 2024), CENT CXL-PIM LLM inference (ASPLOS 2025), Micron Automata Processor, SparQ/Quest top-k attention.

key_insight: Custom HBM4E logic base dies are a real vehicle. Top-k there skips the ~2.5 pJ/bit interposer path for key scans with no array change. It is I-09070's fallback mode.
killer_doubt: Base die gets only ~1x external bandwidth through TSVs, so scan time is unchanged. Saving is ~2.5 pJ/bit on INT4 keys, ~5% of per-token memory energy vs GPU-side Quest.
decisive_experiment: Fold this into the I-09070 simulation as a base-die variant. Synthesize a 128-d INT4 dot-product plus bitonic top-k at 5 nm and confirm under 3% base-die area (<$50k).
prior_art: SK hynix/Samsung custom HBM4 logic base dies. AttAcc. Near-memory attention literature. Quest/SparQ already get the traffic cut in software.

key_insight: A token is 2 B against ~327 KB of KV per token, and idle sessions dominate KV residency. Tiering idle sessions out of HBM is the right lever.
killer_doubt: Re-prefilling 32k tokens on a 70B model is ~4.6e15 FLOP, ~3 kJ per resume. An NVMe reload of the same ~10 GB costs tens of J, so storing wins.
decisive_experiment: Nothing is needed. On one 8-GPU node (<$10k), measure resume energy and latency for recompute versus an LMCache/Mooncake NVMe reload at 8k-128k context.
prior_art: vLLM recompute preemption, HCache (EuroSys 2025), CachedAttention/AttentionStore (ATC 2024), Mooncake, LMCache.

key_insight: Shared system-prompt and agent prefixes make KV highly redundant, and deduplication raises effective capacity 2-5x on those workloads.
killer_doubt: A KV block depends on every earlier token, so the only duplicates are exact prefixes. Software already shares these with no silicon; hardware hashing likely adds <5% capacity.
decisive_experiment: Replay production chat and agent traces (<$20k) and measure the dedup ratio that 4 KB content hashing finds beyond vLLM APC / RadixAttention. Close the idea if the gain is under 5%.
prior_art: vLLM automatic prefix caching, SGLang RadixAttention, HICAMP content-addressed memory (ASPLOS 2012), Linux KSM.

key_insight: Auto-zero/CDS removes comparator offset, the real floor of low-swing links. With E ≈ C·Vswing·Vrail, mm-wire charging falls ~50x. kTC noise on 100 fF is only ~0.2 mV.
killer_doubt: Wire CV² is a minority of the ~2.5 pJ/bit interposer path (1 pF x 0.4 V² ≈ 0.16 pJ). Clocking, PHY and receivers (~30-100 fJ) remain: ~1.5-2x, not 10x.
decisive_experiment: 22/28 nm MPW test chip (~$350k) with 64 CDS low-swing lanes on 3-5 mm interposer-like lines and a switched-capacitor 0.1 V rail. Measure pJ/bit and BER <1e-15 at 4-8 Gb/s against a 0.4 V reference.
prior_art: NVIDIA ground-referenced signaling (~0.54 pJ/bit, 2013). Low-swing on-chip interconnects (Ho/Horowitz). SRAM bitline sensing at 50-100 mV with offset cancellation.

key_insight: For frozen weights, writes and refresh are pure waste. Read-only bits over hybrid bonds give ~0.1 pJ/bit and fab EUV-free in the U.S.
killer_doubt: A 28 nm via-ROM bit is ~0.03-0.06 um2 vs ~0.001 um2 per DRAM cell (30-60x less dense). A 4-bit 70B model needs ~11,000 mm2; ~2.5 GB fits under one die.
decisive_experiment: Nothing is needed. Cost-model the multi-bit ROM-CIM density needed to beat $20/GB DRAM at the bandwidth-per-area of a bonded stack, against Taalas-class hardwired logic (desk study, <$20k).
prior_art: Taalas HC1 hardwires an 8B model on N6 (2026, prior knowledge). ROM-based compute-in-memory literature (2022-25). Classic mask-ROM.
